assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experiments on electron tunnelling through protein media (azurin, cytochrome c, Ru-labelled proteins) turned Marcus theory into a quantitative, distance-dependent physical description of how biological redox chains operate. This is the physical-mechanism approach to respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion that I regard as central to chemistry, and the principles are used well beyond the original proteins.
assessment.attribution: Clean and compact: Gray led the programme and Winkler was the long-term co-developer of the kinetics and tunnelling-pathway analysis. Two names fit comfortably under the three-laureate limit. Priority overlaps with Marcus (already recognised), Hopfield, Beratan and Onuchic on theory, and with other groups on protein-ET experiments; the committee should check that the credit is not simply the experimental side of an already prized theory.
assessment.maturity: Work spans four decades, is reproduced and widely taught. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the age of the principal contributor and the risk that it is seen as an extension of the 1992 Marcus prize are timing concerns.
uncertainties: Whether the 1992 Marcus prize is judged to have already covered the conceptual core.
Whether experimental contributions of other groups on tunnelling pathways (e.g. Dutton, Moser) deserve inclusion; I have not verified their priority claims.
Credit split between Gray and Winkler versus broader ET community is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme that makes biologically available nitrogen and its FeMo-cofactor is one of the most unusual metal clusters in biology. Structures of the cofactor, the interstitial carbide, and recent turnover-state cryo-EM structures link atomic structure to a physical mechanism of multi-electron, multi-proton catalysis, which is exactly the kind of bioenergetic chemistry I value.
assessment.attribution: Decisive structural work: Rees (first structures and carbide/atomic-resolution cofactor), Einsle (carbide identification, high-resolution structures), Seefeldt (mechanism and substrate-reduction chemistry). Dean and Ribbe also contributed genetics and cofactor biosynthesis, so a three-person set leaves out real contributors and the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Structures have been confirmed by many groups for decades. The central mechanism (how N2 binds and is reduced) is still debated, so the interpretation is only partly stable and an award would likely be for structure and cofactor chemistry rather than the full mechanism.
uncertainties: The N2 reduction mechanism is not settled.
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe.
Whether committee would prefer to wait for a mechanistic resolution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical chemistry of how respiratory enzymes, photosystem II and many catalysts move protons and electrons together. Mayer's concerted-PCET thermochemistry and bond-weakening concept, Meyer's early demonstrations, and Hammes-Schiffer's multistate theory made the field quantitative. It is close to my own research area, so I would treat the field as clearly important but be careful about my own bias.
assessment.attribution: Credit is plausible for three but scattered: Meyer (early demonstrations), Mayer (concepts, thermochemistry), Hammes-Schiffer (theory), and Nocera (artificial photosynthesis, PCET in catalysis) are all credible. The discovery is a line of work rather than one clearly attributable discovery, which weakens a clean prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are well established and taught; molecular electrocatalysis applications are still developing. Timing is reasonable but the case rests on field influence more than a single landmark result.
uncertainties: Line of work rather than a single discovery.
Choice among Nocera, Meyer, Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer, and Hammes-Schiffer's theory versus experimental priority.
Potential perception of conflict with my own research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled diffraction-before-destruction structures of radiation-sensitive and microcrystalline proteins at room temperature, and time-resolved studies that watch reactions (e.g. photosystem II, photoactive proteins) in real time. This is the method that makes dynamic mechanisms visible, which I weight strongly.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is difficult: Hajdu and colleagues proposed diffraction before destruction, Chapman and Fromme with collaborators demonstrated SFX in 2011, and Schlichting led time-resolved mixing and photoreceptor work. Neutze, Spence and others also contributed. I would favour Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu for concept and demonstration but this is contestable and Schlichting is a serious alternative.
assessment.maturity: Methodology is widely adopted at multiple XFELs; time-resolved applications are maturing but fewer breakthrough mechanisms have been fully established. Recognition is plausible but possibly slightly early for the dynamics side.
uncertainties: Dispute over who made the decisive conceptual versus experimental contribution.
Impact on chemistry specifically versus physics or structural biology instrumentation.
Whether time-resolved results have matured enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids at defined sites using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It is a general chemical tool for probing and engineering protein function, including mechanisms in enzymes, and is used broadly.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang provided the first eukaryotic and E. coli proof of concept; Chin extended it to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding and organisms. Others (Yokoyama, Mehl) contributed; the three-person selection is defensible but Chin's role relative to Schultz must be weighed.
assessment.maturity: Established for more than two decades and widely adopted; therapeutic applications remain early. Timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl, Yokoyama.
Question of how much of the broader field impact is attributable to the founding experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, a clear example of applying chemical reasoning (deaminase chemistry) to genome engineering and already used clinically. Conceptually original and with high impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly central; Komor and Gaudelli did the cytosine and adenine base-editor work in his lab. Komor and Gaudelli are junior and a prize configuration naming them is unusual. Liu's work on prime editing and other tools also overlaps with other candidates, and CRISPR itself was already recognised in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Discovered 2016-2017; first clinical results are emerging. Strong confirmation of the method, but long-term clinical outcomes are pending, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit Liu alone.
Overlap with CRISPR prize of 2020.
Clinical track record still short.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation uses small molecules that recruit E3 ligases to destroy proteins, including the mechanism by which thalidomide-type molecular glues act through cereblon. It changes how drug discovery thinks about the 'undruggable' proteome and rests on a clear chemical principle.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, with Ito and others. Ciulli, Gray, Kim and Sakamoto also contributed. Allocation across the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Several PROTACs are in late-stage trials but none is approved yet, so clinical validation is incomplete. The mechanistic principles are well confirmed.
uncertainties: Two distinct strands (PROTAC design and molecular glue discovery) may need separate recognition.
No approved PROTAC drug yet.
Credit among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase, so stoichiometry, subunit interactions and membrane protein-lipid complexes can be read directly. It makes macromolecular assemblies, including respiratory complexes, accessible for mechanistic questions.
assessment.attribution: Robinson drove the extension to large complexes and membrane proteins; Heck developed broad application and instrumentation; Chait contributed early protein ESI-MS and complexes. Gross and Loo also contributed, so the three-person limit leaves out valid claims and the 2002 prize (Fenn, Tanaka) overlaps in method.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted over twenty years, though it complements rather than replaces structure methods such as cryo-EM.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 ionization prize.
Unclear fraction of influence attributable to each of the five credited people.
Chemical significance versus structural biology utility.
